A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAPoRL research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original GSM8K and ANLI experiments, cross-domain transfer, heterogeneous-agent evaluations, verifier results, and game-theoretic simulations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds verifier ablations and a trained single-agent RL comparison in Appendix G.7–G.8.

M1.justification: The proposed multi-agent PPO procedure, verifier, reward definitions, collaboration incentives, and QLoRA architecture remain unchanged. Verifier-free and single-agent configurations are introduced as experimental controls.

E1.justification: GSM8K/TinyGSM mathematical reasoning, ANLI inference, reciprocal cross-domain transfer, and the simulated collaboration tasks are retained. The added controls use existing task coverage; different verifier architectures are model configurations.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds a single-agent LLM trained with RL using verifier rewards. Table 7 also compares against verifier-free MAPoRL. These are focused additions to the retained off-the-shelf and supervised-fine-tuning comparisons.

E3.justification: The added controls introduce final-answer-only binary rewards without intermediate feedback, generator–verifier architecture mismatches, and single-turn single-agent RL. Previously reported splits, token limits, agent configurations, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G.7–G.8 substantially expands checks on the source of MAPoRL's gains through verifier removal and trained single-agent RL controls. It also extends the earlier verifier-mismatch observations to reward degradation and generator style drift. These directly examine the roles of reward shaping and joint learning.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the simulations' averaging over 5,000 samples and the SFT temperature checks. V2 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; its added controls report point estimates and qualitative findings.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, transfer, verifier, and interaction-example results are retained. Table 7 newly reports verifier-free GSM8K accuracies of 0.734 and 0.746 on subsequent turns; Table 8 reports single-agent RL accuracy of 0.732 in one turn. Architectural-mismatch findings are also added. These extend results under additional control settings.

T1.justification: The collaboration-game assumptions, Observations 1–2, regularized Nash equilibrium definition, verifier theorem, and proofs are unchanged. Appendix renumbering, a duplicated explanatory remark, and numbering the cumulative-reward equation introduce no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that RL co-training teaches collaboration, improves multi-turn performance, transfers across tasks, and benefits heterogeneous agents. The added controls support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix G.7 interprets gains without verifier shaping as evidence for beneficial co-adaptation under sparse supervision and explains architectural mismatch through degraded rewards and stylistic drift. G.8 emphasizes learning collaboration over maximizing individual accuracy. Existing explicit limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract. Existing architecture descriptions, optimizer and QLoRA settings, hardware information, prompts, and engineering details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Motwani et al. (2024), MALT, to acknowledge verifier–generator–refiner training with DPO, and Liao et al. (2025), MARFT, as a subsequent similar multi-agent RL system. Earlier related-work coverage is retained despite relocation.

P1.justification: The main related-work section moves to Appendix A, with subsequent sections and appendices renumbered. V2 trims verifier/PPO explanations and the conclusion's future-work paragraph, fixes wording and a broken equation reference, and expands acknowledgments. Most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains arrows clarifying information flow, and Tables 7–8 present the added controls. Existing figures and tables are repositioned through page reflow; the original result plots retain their contents and visual design.

improvement.justification: The verifier-free and trained single-agent controls in Tables 7–8 provide useful additional evidence about MAPoRL's gains, and the code link improves access information. The improvement is limited: the architectural-mismatch study remains qualitative, and the single-agent comparison uses one turn against multi-turn collaboration, leaving the mechanism only partially isolated.
